description: Sign-in required: call connect(email) and connect_verify first (free, one email) unless this connection is already signed in. What changed in an act (or one article) between two dates: the version in force on from_date (the baseline) against the one on to_date, and every change that took effect in between, each with its own įsigaliojimo data. Any window works. Returns version metadata and register links. With `article`, held editions also supply its wording on both dates and a word-level redline; missing wording is reported as not held, never reconstructed from register notes.

act_number.description: Alternative to document_id: the act number or code (`VIII-1864`, `CK`). A list (`['DK','CK','XI-2159']` or `DK, CK, XI-2159`, up to 20) checks every act's window in one call, one compact row each under `acts` (no `article` then).
act_number.title: Act Number

amended_by.description: Optional amending act number (`XV-1058`): with no `article`, keep only the articles whose new wording the register credits to that act - 'what does this amendment change'.
amended_by.title: Amended By

article.description: Optional article (`1.125`, `57`, or `58 str. 3 d. 4 p.` for one point): its wording on both dates and a word-level redline (`[-deleted-]`, `{+inserted+}`) where the act's editions are held, plus its own changes in the window from the register's notes. A list (`['57','65','89']` or `57, 65, 89`, up to 25) answers each under `articles` in one call. Without `article` the answer lists EVERY article whose words changed in the window (`articles_changed`, with shortened redlines).
article.title: Article

detail.description: `compact` (the default for a list of articles or a whole act): per article whether it changed, both wordings' dates, the edits and the changed paragraphs - no whole wordings. `full` (the default for one article) adds each article's wording on both dates and the marked text.
detail.title: Detail

document_id.description: The act to compare, by search hit id. An article id (with `#`) resolves to its act.
document_id.title: Document Id

from_date.description: The earlier date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (a contract date, say). The version in force on it is the baseline; any date works.
from_date.title: From Date

jurisdiction.description: Which jurisdiction the act belongs to (`LT`). Omit for the account's own.
jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction

session.description: The `session` value the sign-in returned. Pass it on every call in this conversation, so the sign-in survives however this client handles connections; omit it when the user connected with Sign in (OAuth) or a key.

to_date.description: The later date, `YYYY-MM-DD` (today, say). Must be on or after from_date.
to_date.title: To Date

name: compare_provision_versions
title: Versions between two dates
